paper_id: Revealing Task Driven Knowledge Worker Behaviors in Open Source Software Communities
title: Revealing Task Driven Knowledge Worker Behaviors in Open Source Software Communities
motivation: Open-source software dominates modern IT systems, but how developers behave under workload stress remains unclear
problem_framing: Empirically quantify developer behavioral changes when transitioning from normal to overload working states
key_insight: Developers exhibit opposite behavioral patterns in spatial vs temporal scale when overloaded; processing times follow stretched exponential, not power law
method_signature: Empirical analysis of Eclipse/Mozilla bug-tracking data with workload-performance curve fitting and Kruskal-Wallis tests
evaluation_criteria: 99% confidence intervals for curve fitting; Kruskal-Wallis H test at 0.01 significance; Vuong closeness test for distribution comparison
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Cannot precisely describe developers' true states due to lack of real behavioral data; intrinsic relationships between spatial and temporal behavior remain unknown
evidence_for_taste: work overload is observed during the collaborative SDR activities
a fundamental issue in developer behavior analysis is still unclear
which differs from the previous findings on the timing of human behavior
the phenomenon of work overload is observed
We have to admit that the working states presented here cannot describe developers' true states precisely
the intrinsic relationships between developer's spatial behavior and temporal behavior remain unknown
thinking_moves: 从绩效曲线拐点反推工作负荷阈值的存在
把开发者行为分解为空间尺度(队列位置)和时间尺度(处理时长)两个维度
用二阶导数趋近零的条件形式化定义稳态/过载转变点
对比前人power-law发现, 用Vuong检验证明stretched exponential更优
跨两个OSS社区(Eclipse/Mozilla)验证行为模式一致性
